classes.name: House of Representatives general elections
classes.locator: https://www.legislation.gov.au/C1918A00027/latest/text (Part XVIII; s 274: preferential voting in single-member divisions)
classes.note: Single-member divisions. First past the post (in most states) at the elections of 1901-1917; preferential (instant-runoff) voting since the Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918, first at the 1919 general election; Tasmania voted as one five-member electorate in 1901. Terms run at most three years from the first sitting (Constitution s 28), so elections are called, sometimes after a double dissolution (s 57). 48 general elections 1901-2025; 75 members in 1901, 150 in 2025.

classes.name: Senate elections
classes.locator: https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004Q00685/latest/text (ss 7, 13: senators for each state chosen by the people of the state voting as one electorate, half retiring every three years)
classes.note: Each state votes as one electorate, half its senators every three years and all of them after a double dissolution; the territories elect two senators each since 1975. Block (plurality, then preferential) voting until 1946; single transferable vote since 1949, with above-the-line group tickets 1984-2013 and optional preferences above the line since 2016. Popular elections to fill casual vacancies were held in South Australia (1908) and Queensland (1963) before the 1977 amendment of s 15.

classes.name: ACT Legislative Assembly general elections

Fixed terms: the third Saturday in October every fourth year since 2001. No by-elections: vacancies are filled by countback (s 194). The ACT has no local government; the territory government performs municipal functions.
